reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about microstructural control via deposition technique and the mechanism of creep resistance, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers dislocation-interface interactions generally, but the specific link to thermal spray/cladding of FCC/BCC HEAs and its dominance over other factors requires cited support, which is absent.
premises: Thermal spray/cladding produces heterogeneous FCC/BCC phase boundaries in HEA coatings
Phase boundaries act as obstacles to dislocation glide and climb
Dislocation hindrance by interfaces reduces creep strain rate
Homogeneous microstructures lack such effective dislocation barriers
